title: China's First Large Model 3.0 Pro in the Chemical Industry is Officially Released, Marking a Shift from Answering to Executing

content_html:
The Chinese chemical industry has achieved a milestone breakthrough in intelligent transformation. On August 31, the Dalian Institute of Chemical Physics of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, in collaboration with leading institutions such as iFLYTEK and Alibaba Cloud, officially released the latest iteration of China's first large model in the chemical industry - the Intelligent Chemical Industry Large Model 3.0 Pro. This major upgrade marks a significant leap for industry large models from traditional "professional knowledge Q&A" to an "intelligent execution system for chemical tasks."

As an innovative achievement at the technology foundation level, this version has advanced large models from merely "being able to understand and answer" to a new stage of "being able to plan, execute, and verify." It is no longer just a professional assistant for knowledge acquisition, but has officially upgraded to become an "intelligent engineering partner" that can collaborate with professional researchers to complete complex tasks, injecting new momentum into the intelligence of chemical research and development, engineering design, and production operations.

In terms of research and development models and system construction, the Intelligent Chemical Industry Large Model 3.0 Pro breaks away from the conventional application mode of traditional large models that focus on knowledge Q&A and content generation. It innovatively builds a four-layer technical system: "large model - intelligent agent - professional skills and tools - application scenarios." This full-chain architecture enables it to have stronger scenario implementation and practical engineering processing capabilities.

According to rigorous testing by the multidimensional evaluation system of the chemical industry, the core performance of this version has made a significant leap forward. The text question-answering accuracy rate and multimodal question-answering accuracy rate reached 81.96% and 80.75%, respectively. The comprehensive score increased by 20.2% and 31.4% compared to the previous 3.0 version, fully demonstrating its strong practical value in professional fields.
